posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
We played Challenge Mode Omnitron 5 times at home (H=4) and got wrecked every time.  As a result, the Statistics Project currently shows him as the toughest villain overall.  Let's get more data!

I think 4 is the worst, it's enough to get out all the components, and the damage is plenty.  I finally beat him in the app using the cheesiest party I could assemble: Greatest Legacy, TLT, Scholar, Haka, Wraith.  If not for Sedative Flechettes the round I played Ground Pound, I would have taken almost no damage past round 1.  As it was, everyone ended in single digit HP, with Haka at 1.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked: Oof, you ain't kidding that Challenge Cosmitron is brutal -- but doable. Took a (mostly) randomized group of OX, Parse, Santa Guise, Ra and Unity against him, in Dok'Thorath. Both copies of Technological Singularity came out early enough they didn't do much damage and OX was able to get another Component into play to keep him from flipping. Parse was able to Buffer Overflow away a set of Flechettes that would've killed the team outright, and a double-play of S-84s dropped Parse and Unity down to 1 HP and a final furious round of damage (and a redirect of one of those S-84s by the total Beefcake) finished him off.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked: I beat Ultimate Cosmitron without OX - my team was Legacy, ChronoRanger, Parse, Hunted Naturalist, and KNYFE in Insula Primalis. The trick is to assume that you won’t survive Cosmitron’s third turn, so just try and deal 100 damage in two rounds.

It really is. It takes a bit of luck, but Legacy, Parse, ChronoRanger, Naturalist, and Insula Primalis all have damage multipliers, and ChronoRanger and KNYFE can many instances of damage in a turn.

You do have to avoid the 10 hp drones and the Disruptive Fletchettes, but that’s about all.
